items.title: Nepal flood toll rises to 1,252 as at least 4,216 remain unaccounted for
items.blurb: NDRRMA noon figures. Nearly 900 hydropower workers still missing. 11,913 rescued.

items.title: Bhotekoshi floods expose gaps in Nepal’s emergency communications
items.blurb: Most towers are back, but fibre is gone in places and calls still drop. The post-2015 disaster communications plan was never fully enacted.

items.title: Oft-battered Langtang Valley cut off after Rasuwa floods
items.blurb: No road from Syabrubesi to Dhunche. Tourists and supplies depend on helicopters.

items.title: Nepal sent its disaster alert 38 minutes after the glacier collapse
items.blurb: The warning came after the collapse, raising questions about high-mountain monitoring and early warning.

items.title: Fourteen minutes before the flood hit, a warning sent 900 students running
items.blurb: A warning helped clear Tribhuvan Trishuli Secondary School in Bidur before the flood reached the area.

items.title: UN Women estimates 43,000 women and girls need urgent assistance
items.blurb: Women and girls in Rasuwa and Nuwakot face urgent needs including food, water and protection.

items.title: Local governments take charge of flood relief
items.blurb: Local committees in Rasuwa and Nuwakot are taking a larger role in relief operations.

items.title: Nepal seeks urgent climate finance after Bhotekoshi flood
items.blurb: The government is seeking immediate support through international loss-and-damage financing.

items.title: In Nepal’s flood zone, the second disaster is psychological
items.blurb: Mental-health teams are beginning to reach survivors as recovery continues.

items.title: The floods keep coming. Nepal keeps starting over
items.blurb: The latest disaster has renewed questions about preparedness, response and long-term resilience.

items.title: Reconstruction could cost up to $5 billion
items.blurb: The government is assessing the damage while relief remains the immediate priority.
